rounds.text: [E1] (bear) Trades at a P/E of 169x implies that Amber Enterprises India Ltd's stock is significantly overvalued compared to its sector benchmark of 32.71x. This suggests that investors are paying an extremely high price for each rupee of earnings, which carries substantial risk. [E4] (bear) A dividend yield of 0.00% indicates that the company does not distribute any profits to shareholders through dividends, further diminishing its appeal as a growth investment option. [E5] (neutral) The stock's current position within its historical price range suggests it is trading at a moderate level, neither significantly undervalued nor overvalued based on recent performance alone. [E44] (bear) A discounted cash flow analysis indicates that the intrinsic value of Amber Enterprises India Ltd is only Rs 1686 per share, which is far below its current market price of Rs 7209. This leaves a margin of safety of -327.5%, indicating significant overvaluation. [E45] (bear) The negative margin of safety further supports the notion that Amber Enterprises India Ltd's stock may be overvalued, as it implies that the company is trading at a premium to its intrinsic value. [E46] (bear) A reverse discounted cash flow analysis suggests that the current price already implies 38.7% earnings growth, which is significantly higher than the base case assumption of 18.0%. This further reinforces the idea that the stock may be overvalued given its historical performance and future expectations. [E55] (neutral) Despite profit growth outpacing share price growth by 24% versus a 19% increase in the last five years, this could indicate potential undervaluation if the company is not fully capturing market appreciation. However, without additional context on the sector's performance and competitive landscape, it remains neutral. Conceded: [E7] (bear) P/B of 5.87x against a sector benchmark of 2.76x suggests that Amber Enterprises India Ltd may be overvalued compared to its peers in terms of book value per share.
